title: Smooth-proper datum
statement: Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$, with $k_0=\Fq$ and $k=\Fbar$ its fixed algebraic closure. A *smooth-proper datum* $\mathscr X=(X_0,d,X)$ consists of a $k_0$-scheme $X_0$ that is smooth, proper and geometrically connected, an integer $d\geq0$ such that $X_0$ is smooth of pure dimension $d$ (its structure morphism is smooth and every irreducible component of $X_0\times_{k_0}k$ has dimension $d$), and the geometric fiber $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. When $X_0$ and $d$ are given, 'the resulting smooth-proper datum' is $(X_0,d,X_0\times_{k_0}k)$. Every object later defined from $\mathscr X$ (the cohomological family, the Frobenius characteristic factors, the canonical integral factors, the Betti numbers, the determinant constants, the Euler characteristic and the functional-equation sign) is a function of $\mathscr X$, even when that argument is suppressed.
